 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. South Africa and Australia will face off in the third and final Test from October 27 at Newlands in Cape Town, with both sides level at 1-1.
 Australia beat South Africa in the first Test at Durban by 214 runs, but South Africa staged a comeback and won the second Test at Gqeberha by and innings and 31 runs.

 Temba Bavuma and Marco Jansen were crucial in South Africa's win in the second Test, but the hosts will have to find a replacement for the injured Anrich Nortje. Australia, on the other hand, will need their batters to play better after Travis Head's second-innings century offered some resistance.
 Both sides will depend on their fast bowlers at Newlands, where South Africa will attempt to win the series while Australia will be trying to regain the lead in the decider.
 The Sporting News has all you need to know about South Africa vs. Australia 3rd Test, including date, time, and how and where to watch it.

 South Africa vs. Australia 3rd Test live stream, TV channel
 Here's how to watch South Africa vs. Australia 3rd Test live in India:
 TV channel: Eurosport TV Network
 Live stream: FanCode
 In India, the Eurosport TV Network will telecast the series, with live streaming available through FanCode app and website.
 MORE: Visit Cricket News for all the latest cricket coverage and opinion 
 What time does South Africa vs. Australia 3rd Test start?
 The third Test between South Africa and Australia will be played at Newlands in Cape Town, South Africa.
 Play is scheduled to begin at 10:30 a.m. local time (SAST), which translates to 2:00 p.m. IST on Tuesday, October 27 , for viewers in India .

 South Africa vs. Australia 3rd Test team news, lineups
 South Africa will be without fast bowler Anrich Nortje, who has been ruled out with a groin injury. Gerald Coetzee, Corbin Bosch, Dane Paterson and spinner Keshav Maharaj are options to replace him. Ryan Rickelton is expected to retain the wicketkeeping role after the second Test win.
 South Africa confirmed XI: Aiden Markram, Marques Ackerman, David Bedingham, Temba Bavuma (c), Matthew Breetzke, Ryan Rickelton (wk), Wiaan Mulder, Marco Jansen, Simon Harmer, Kagiso Rabada, Gerald Coetzee.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Australia released Nic Maddinson and Sam Harper to play in the Sheffield Shield. Cameron Green is available as a specialist batter, while Josh Inglis is also in contention. Steve Smith faces a fitness test for his neck issue, and Australia must decide whether to include Nathan Lyon or retain Scott Boland.
 Australia predicted XI: Travis Head, Matthew Renshaw, Marnus Labuschagne, Steve Smith, Cameron Green, Alex Carey (wk), Josh Inglis, Pat Cummins (c), Mitchell Starc, Scott Boland, Josh Hazlewood.
